# Monitoring, validation and plausibility checks for web scraped data {#Monitoringvalidationandplausibilitychecksforwebscrapeddata-Monitoringvalidationandplausibilitychecksforwebscrapeddata}

Contrary to scanner data where the data sets are stored by the retailers
and backup files are available, web collection does not allow recovery
of past data. Hence, caution should be taken to evaluate if the
collection is being performed appropriately to minimize and avoid
mistakes and data losses.

Automatic monitoring of data collection is advisable especially when
performing bulk web scraping where timely identification of problems is
more challenging. It is useful to build a monitoring dashboard with
automatic checks for control and validation of the extracted data.
Useful checks noted within Eurostat\'s HICP - \"[Practical guidelines on
web scraping for the
HICP](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/272892/12032198/Guidelines-web-scraping-HICP-11-2020.pdf/)\"
include the following

- check if data size agrees with previous collections
- check if the list of datasets and attributes are as expected
- check for duplicate records
- check the total number of items and levels of product churn each month
- check number of items found which have values equal to zero
- checks for suspicious values and outliers, and
- checks for the number of items that were not classified.

Whenever possible, automatic solution to problems identified is
advisable and a report with the mistakes found should be generated
allowing further analysis of the main problems by experts (Ref. (2)).
Early identification allows faster actions and reduces the impact of the
problems for Consumer Price Index (CPI) compilation.

Section 5 of Eurostat\'s HICP - \"[Practical guidelines on web scraping
for the
HICP](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/272892/12032198/Guidelines-web-scraping-HICP-11-2020.pdf/)\"
and section 4.3 of Ref. (1) provide more details and experiences on the
subject.
